title: The Lancet: "AstraZeneca must retreat"
description: The Lancet’s editor accused AstraZeneca of marketing the new statin with "adventurous statistics" before its research was complete, and urged doctors to pause before prescribing it. AstraZeneca called the editorial flawed and incorrect.

title: Petition to ban it
description: The consumer group Public Citizen asked the FDA to take Crestor off the market, citing reports of muscle breakdown and kidney damage. The FDA kept it on sale.

title: Its landmark trial was stopped early
description: The JUPITER trial was stopped for benefit after less than two years. Critics in the Archives of Internal Medicine argued that stopping early exaggerated the benefit, and noted that 9 of its 14 authors had financial ties to the sponsor.

title: Sued the FDA to keep generics out
description: AstraZeneca argued that a seven-year "orphan drug" exclusivity, earned for a rare inherited cholesterol disorder in children, should block every generic. A judge refused, and generics launched in the US in 2016.

title: Texas Medicaid settlement
description: $20 million of a $110 million settlement with Texas was over allegedly misrepresenting Crestor’s benefits. AstraZeneca denied wrongdoing.

title: Ads pulled after a congressional inquiry
description: Pfizer cancelled TV ads starring Robert Jarvik, an artificial-heart inventor who was not licensed to practise medicine, after members of Congress questioned them. A stunt double had done his rowing.

title: Generic recalled for glass particles
description: Ranbaxy, a generic maker, recalled 41 lots of its atorvastatin after finding tiny glass particles. No injuries were reported. Ranbaxy pleaded guilty to US felony charges over its factories the following year.

title: Diabetes lawsuits thrown out
description: More than 3,000 women sued, saying Pfizer failed to warn that Lipitor could cause diabetes. The court ruled their expert evidence unreliable, and in 2018 the appeals court upheld Pfizer’s win.
sources: US District Court, MDL 2502 <https://www.scd.uscourts.gov/mdlipitor/current.asp>; Washington Legal Foundation (2018) <https://www.wlf.org/case/in-re-lipitor-marketing-sales-practices-and-products-liability-litigation/>

title: Pay-for-delay settlements
description: US buyers said Pfizer’s 2008 patent deal with Ranbaxy delayed cheaper generic Lipitor. Pfizer settled in 2024, paying $93 million to wholesalers and $35 million to consumers and insurers.
sources: Bloomberg Law (2024) <https://news.bloomberglaw.com/ip-law/pfizer-settles-lipitor-antitrust-lawsuit-with-93-million-payout>; Law360 via Cohen Milstein (2024) <https://www.cohenmilstein.com/lipitor-buyers-seek-final-ok-for-35m-deal-in-antitrust-fight/>

maker: Byk Gulden (now Takeda); sold in the US by Wyeth, now Pfizer
title: Hid discounts from Medicaid
description: Wyeth was alleged to have hidden deep discounts it gave hospitals on Protonix from Medicaid’s "best price" calculation, underpaying the rebates it owed. Wyeth and Pfizer paid $784.6 million.

maker: Byk Gulden (now Takeda); sold in the US by Wyeth, now Pfizer
title: Kidney-injury lawsuits settled
description: Thousands of US lawsuits claimed that acid-suppressing PPIs caused kidney disease. Pfizer, which sold Protonix in the US, settled before AstraZeneca’s $425 million deal in 2023. Its amount was not disclosed.

title: The "chiral switch"
description: Esomeprazole is one of the two mirror-image forms that make up AstraZeneca’s older omeprazole (Losec, or Prilosec in the US). It was launched as omeprazole’s patent ran out, and patients were moved across with heavy marketing. A 2022 case study calls it a textbook evergreening strategy.

title: EU fine over the older drug’s patents
description: The European Commission found AstraZeneca gave patent offices "deliberately misleading" information to extend protection for omeprazole, the drug Nexium replaced, and withdrew products to block generics. The fine was €52.5 million after appeal.

title: Jury: a "large and unjustified" payment
description: In a US pay-for-delay trial, the jury found AstraZeneca’s 2008 deal with the generic maker Ranbaxy involved a large and unjustified payment, but not that it delayed generic Nexium, so no damages were awarded. The appeals court upheld the verdict in 2016.

title: Kickbacks for formulary placement
description: AstraZeneca settled allegations that it cut prices on other drugs for Medco, a pharmacy-benefit manager, in return for Nexium being the only PPI on Medco’s lists. The case began as a whistleblower suit by two former employees.

title: Kidney-injury lawsuits
description: AstraZeneca paid $425 million to settle US lawsuits claiming Nexium and Prilosec caused kidney disease. It said the claims were without merit.

maker: Lundbeck; sold in the US by Forest Laboratories, now AbbVie
title: Teen approval leaned on a disputed trial
description: The FDA approved Lexapro for 12 to 17-year-olds partly on the strength of a positive trial of its parent drug, citalopram (study MD-18). A 2016 analysis of court documents called the published report of that trial ghostwritten and said it mischaracterised the data.
sources: Fierce Biotech (2009) <https://www.fiercebiotech.com/biotech/forest-laboratories-inc-announces-fda-approval-of-lexapro-r-for-treatment-of-major>; Int. J. Risk & Safety in Medicine (2016) <https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.3233/JRS-160671>

maker: Lundbeck; sold in the US by Forest Laboratories, now AbbVie
title: Guilty plea and kickbacks
description: Forest pleaded guilty to obstruction of justice, distributing an unapproved thyroid drug and promoting Celexa for children. The $313 million total also settled claims that it paid kickbacks (cash disguised as grants and consulting fees, meals and entertainment) to boost Celexa and Lexapro prescriptions.

maker: Lundbeck; sold in the US by Forest Laboratories, now AbbVie
title: EU fine: paying generics to stay out
description: The European Commission fined Lundbeck about €94 million for paying generic makers in 2002 to stay out of the market for citalopram, the older drug of which escitalopram is the active half. The EU’s top court upheld the fines in 2021.

title: A new salt
description: Servier switched Coversyl to a new form, perindopril arginine. Australia’s NPS said it was more stable in hot climates and equivalent in the body. NHS reviewers in England found no clinically significant benefit over the cheaper generic, and critics called it evergreening.

title: NHS damages claim, still running
description: The NHS in England sued Servier in 2011 for the extra it paid while cheaper generic perindopril was kept off the market, a claim put at more than £250 million. Servier lost key preliminary arguments in 2022 and on appeal in 2023, and the case was still active in 2026.
sources: The Pharma Letter (2022) <https://www.thepharmaletter.com/generics-news/setback-for-servier-in-generic-delay-case-claimed-to-have-cost-the-nhs-250-million>; Monckton Chambers (2023) <https://www.monckton.com/servier-pay-for-delay-litigation-monckton-success-for-nhs-in-the-court-of-appeal/>; Global Competition Review (2026) <https://globalcompetitionreview.com/article/uk-tribunal-rejects-nhs-evidence-request-in-pay-delay-damages-claim>

title: EU fine: paying generics to stay out
description: Between 2005 and 2007, whenever a generic maker came close to launching, Servier settled with it, with cash payments running to tens of millions of euros. The European Commission fined Servier €331 million and five generic companies €97 million. The General Court cut Servier’s fine to €228 million in 2018, and the EU Court of Justice largely upheld the case in 2024.

title: Ghostwritten science
description: A Pfizer document disclosed in litigation listed 85 sertraline papers being coordinated by a medical-writing agency. Healy and Cattell found agency-linked papers made up 55 of the 96 sertraline articles of 1998–2000, and were cited about five times as often as the rest.
sources: Healy & Cattell, Br J Psychiatry (2003) <https://doi.org/10.1192/bjp.183.1.22>; BMJ Open (figure) <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4120312/figure/BMJOPEN2013004777F2>

title: Birth-defect lawsuits thrown out
description: Families claimed Zoloft taken in pregnancy caused birth defects. The court excluded their experts’ evidence as unreliable and ended more than 300 cases, and in 2017 the appeals court upheld Pfizer’s win.

title: Carcinogen contamination in the US
description: In May 2020 the FDA asked five companies, including Teva and Apotex, to recall extended-release metformin after finding high levels of NDMA, a probable carcinogen. More makers followed.

title: And in Australia
description: TGA testing found about 30% of batches slightly above the acceptable NDMA limit (under twice the limit) and one batch at 4.4 times the limit, which was recalled. The TGA judged the risk low and told patients not to stop taking metformin.

maker: Eli Lilly originally; now many generic makers
title: Nothing significant found

maker: Beecham (now GSK) originally; now many generic makers
title: Nothing significant found
A wall of patents
description: The patent-reform group I-MAK counted 129 patent applications on Keytruda, 74% of them not for the active ingredient, and estimated they could extend Merck’s monopoly by eight years or more beyond 2028.

title: Senate tax inquiry
description: The chair of the US Senate Finance Committee said Merck booked Keytruda’s profits offshore, holding the rights in the Netherlands and making it in Ireland: 46% of its 2021 sales were in the US but only 14% of its pre-tax income. Merck said it had cooperated.

title: The "product hop"
description: Merck launched an under-the-skin version, Keytruda Qlex. I-MAK called it a product hop: moving patients to a newly patented form before the original’s patents expire.

title: Price, patents and dose
description: An April 2026 investigation by the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists found 50 active US patents that could protect Keytruda until at least 2042, and list prices from about US$80,000 a year in Germany to US$208,000 in the US. Researchers it consulted said Merck promotes a higher dose than necessary.

title: Price v cost of making it
description: A 2022 study estimated a year’s supply could be made for about US$5,700, against a US list price of about US$325,000. The estimate covers manufacturing only, not research.
sources: Guo et al., J Cyst Fibros (2022) <https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35440408/>

title: South African competition probe
description: South Africa’s Competition Commission investigated Vertex from 2022 over alleged excessive pricing and refusal to supply. It closed the case in December 2024 after Vertex gave undertakings, and patient groups asked in 2025 for it to be reopened.

title: Insurers’ antitrust class action
description: US health insurers sued in December 2023, alleging J&J kept biosimilars off the market with a patent they say was wrongly granted and by buying a rival’s patents. The court certified a class in December 2025. In January 2026 it ruled for J&J on the patent-purchase claim, but the rest of the case continues. J&J is contesting it.

title: An FDA safety signal
description: In March 2025 the FDA listed cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, a rare cancer that can look like eczema, as a potential risk it was evaluating. Studies disagree: some found many more reports than expected, and at least one large study found no increased risk.

title: Lymphoma lawsuits
description: The first suits were filed in 2025. In June 2026 about 30 federal cases claiming Dupixent caused or worsened T-cell lymphoma were grouped before one judge in New Jersey, with more in state court and a proposed class action in Maryland. Sanofi says it cannot yet assess the outcome.
sources: Sanofi half-year report (2026) <https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001121404/000162828026050803/sny-20260630_d2.htm>; Regeneron quarterly report (2026) <https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000872589/000087258926000025/regn-20260630.htm>; AboutLawsuits (2026) <https://www.aboutlawsuits.com/dupixent-lawsuit/dupixent-injection-lawsuits-consolidated-mdl-ctcl-diagnoses/>

title: Kickbacks through a copay charity
description: The US government alleges Regeneron gave tens of millions of dollars in 2013–14 to a supposedly independent charity to cover Medicare patients’ Eylea copays, an illegal kickback. A 2025 appeals ruling made such cases harder to prove, but the case continues. Regeneron says it has no merit.
sources: STAT (2020) <https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2020/06/24/regeneron-kickbacks-medicare-foundations/>; US Court of Appeals, 1st Cir. (2025) <https://www.ca1.uscourts.gov/sites/ca1/files/opnfiles/23-2086P-01A.pdf>; Regeneron quarterly report (2026) <https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000872589/000087258926000025/regn-20260630.htm>

title: Inflating Medicare’s price
description: The Justice Department alleges Regeneron hid hundreds of millions of dollars of credit-card-fee payments to distributors that should have lowered Eylea’s reported average price, inflating what Medicare paid from 2012 to 2023. It began as a whistleblower suit. A judge refused to dismiss it in 2025; Regeneron says the claims are without merit.
sources: US DOJ (2024) <https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/false-claims-act-complaint-filed-against-regeneron-pharmaceuticals-fraudulent-drug-pricing>; Court order via Endpoints (2025) <https://endpoints.news/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/regeneronfalseclaimsorder.pdf>

maker: Purdue Pharma; Mundipharma outside the US
title: Lied about addiction risk
description: Purdue’s parent company and three executives pleaded guilty to misbranding OxyContin as less addictive and less prone to abuse than other opioids.

maker: Purdue Pharma; Mundipharma outside the US
title: Second guilty plea: three felonies
description: Purdue pleaded guilty to three federal felonies, including conspiring to defraud the US and paying kickbacks. Most of the $8.3 billion was an unsecured claim in bankruptcy and was never paid in full.

maker: Purdue Pharma; Mundipharma outside the US
title: Australia: misleading Targin ads
description: After an addiction specialist complained, the TGA found Mundipharma’s Targin advertising to GPs "misleading, imbalanced and otherwise inaccurate" and issued 24 infringement notices.

maker: Purdue Pharma; Mundipharma outside the US
title: Bankruptcy plan approved
description: A US court approved Purdue’s bankruptcy plan, under which the Sackler family pays up to $6.5 billion over 15 years.

maker: Many makers; Allergan (now AbbVie) sold Norco
title: Allergan opioid settlement
description: Allergan, former maker of Norco and Kadian, agreed to pay up to $2.37 billion to US states and localities over its opioid marketing.

title: Fentanyl "lollipop" promoted off-label
description: Cephalon pleaded guilty to promoting Actiq, a fentanyl lozenge meant only for cancer pain, and two other drugs for unapproved uses.

title: Bribes for fentanyl spray
description: Insys paid doctors through sham "speaker programmes" to prescribe Subsys. Founder John Kapoor was convicted of racketeering conspiracy and jailed.

title: J&J’s national opioid settlement
description: J&J, maker of Durogesic patches, agreed to pay up to $5 billion over its opioid business, admitting no wrongdoing.

title: Reckitt’s record opioid settlement
description: Reckitt Benckiser paid $1.4 billion, then the largest opioid-related settlement, over the marketing of Suboxone.

title: False child-safety data
description: Indivior pleaded guilty to a felony. It admitted sending Massachusetts Medicaid false data claiming its Suboxone film had the lowest rate of accidental child exposure.

title: Tooth-decay lawsuits
description: Thousands of US lawsuits claiming the film dissolved under the tongue caused severe tooth decay were grouped in an Ohio federal court. The first trial is reportedly set for 2028.

title: The truncated CLASS trial
description: The 2000 JAMA paper claimed fewer stomach ulcers than older painkillers, using six months of data from two longer trials. Critics in the BMJ showed the full data, which the FDA had, did not support the advantage. The authors defended their choice.

title: Investors: heart risks concealed
description: Pfizer settled a class action by investors who said it concealed the cardiovascular risks of its COX-2 painkillers, Celebrex and Bextra.

title: Off-label promotion
description: Pfizer’s record settlement included civil claims that it promoted Lyrica, along with Geodon and Zyvox, for unapproved uses.

title: Off-label campaign
description: Warner-Lambert pleaded guilty. Neurontin had been promoted for bipolar disorder, pain and migraine, partly through paid "consultant" meetings.

title: Switched trial outcomes
description: Comparing internal documents with publications, researchers found that 8 of 12 published trials reported a different primary outcome from the protocol, and unfavourable results were reported with a changed outcome or not in full. Pfizer disputed the findings.

title: Racketeering verdict
description: A federal jury found Pfizer ran a racketeering enterprise to market Neurontin. Damages for the insurer Kaiser were trebled to $142 million.

maker: Many makers; Tylenol by McNeil (J&J), now Kenvue
title: Metal particles in children’s Tylenol
description: McNeil pleaded guilty after shipping infants’ and children’s liquid medicines contaminated with metal particles. Prosecutors said it knew of the problem for about a year.

maker: Many makers; Tylenol by McNeil (J&J), now Kenvue
title: Autism lawsuits revived
description: A judge threw out hundreds of US cases claiming paracetamol in pregnancy caused autism or ADHD after excluding the plaintiffs’ experts. In July 2026 an appeals court revived them, without finding that paracetamol causes autism. The defendants sought a rehearing.

maker: Many makers; Tylenol by McNeil (J&J), now Kenvue
title: FDA caution in pregnancy
description: The FDA said it would update the label about a possible association with autism, while acknowledging that a causal relationship had not been established. Sibling studies that control for family factors found no increased risk.

title: New York sues over hidden child trials
description: New York’s Attorney General accused GSK of suppressing studies showing Paxil did not work in children and might raise suicidality. GSK settled and agreed to post its trial results online.

title: Guilty plea: promoting Paxil to under-18s
description: GSK pleaded guilty to misbranding Paxil, including promoting it for under-18s, as part of a $3 billion settlement.

title: Study 329 reanalysed
description: An independent reanalysis of the 2001 trial found paroxetine no better than placebo for adolescent depression, with clinically significant increases in harms including suicidal thoughts and behaviour. The original paper had claimed the opposite.

title: UK: paying generics to stay out
description: The UK regulator found GSK paid would-be generic rivals more than £50 million in 2001–04 to stay out of the market. When generics arrived, prices fell 70%.

title: A buried weight-gain study
description: Court-released emails showed an AstraZeneca manager complaining about "cherry-picking" data and listing buried trials, including Study 15, in which patients gained weight. AstraZeneca said the FDA had reviewed the safety data.

title: Off-label for sleep, anger and dementia
description: Then the largest civil-only off-label settlement, covering promotion for aggression, Alzheimer’s, anger management, anxiety, ADHD, dementia and sleeplessness.

title: Texas Medicaid settlement
description: $90 million of a $110 million Texas settlement was over off-label Seroquel promotion. AstraZeneca denied wrongdoing.

title: Weight-gain and diabetes lawsuits
description: About 32,000 claims said Lilly played down Zyprexa’s links to obesity and diabetes, after internal documents were leaked to the New York Times.

title: Guilty plea: off-label for dementia
description: Lilly pleaded guilty to promoting Zyprexa for elderly dementia and other unapproved uses.

title: Guilty plea and kickbacks
description: Janssen pleaded guilty to misbranding Risperdal, which had been promoted for elderly dementia patients and children, and paid kickbacks to doctors and a nursing-home pharmacy.

title: Breast-growth lawsuits
description: About 9,000 lawsuits said boys developed breasts on Risperdal. A Philadelphia jury awarded $8 billion in punitive damages in one case, cut by a judge to $6.8 million; J&J then settled substantially all the cases, setting aside $800 million.

maker: Otsuka and Bristol Myers Squibb (now generic)
title: Off-label promotion and kickbacks
description: BMS settled claims including promotion of Abilify for children and dementia-related psychosis, consulting fees and resort trips for doctors, and inflated wholesale prices.

maker: Otsuka and Bristol Myers Squibb (now generic)
title: Compulsive gambling lawsuits
description: BMS and Otsuka reached a confidential master settlement of US claims that Abilify caused compulsive gambling and other behaviours, disclaiming liability.

maker: Lundbeck; sold in the US by Forest (now AbbVie)
title: Guilty plea: promoting Celexa for children
description: Forest pleaded guilty, including to promoting Celexa for children, and settled claims it paid kickbacks to boost Celexa and Lexapro.

maker: Lundbeck; sold in the US by Forest (now AbbVie)
title: EU fine: paying generics to stay out
description: The European Commission fined Lundbeck for paying generic makers in 2002 to stay out of the citalopram market. The EU’s top court upheld it in 2021.

maker: Lundbeck; sold in the US by Forest (now AbbVie)
title: A ghostwritten child trial
description: An analysis of court documents called the published report of the paediatric trial MD-18 ghostwritten and said it mischaracterised the data.
sources: Int. J. Risk & Safety in Medicine (2016) <https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.3233/JRS-160671>

title: Australia: injunctions on an invalid patent
description: Wyeth won court orders in 2009 blocking three generic suppliers; the patent was later overturned. The generic companies sued on Wyeth’s undertaking to pay for any harm, and the Federal Court upheld their claims in 2018. The Commonwealth, which had overpaid through the PBS, settled its own claim.

title: Guilty plea: off-label Wellbutrin
description: GSK pleaded guilty to promoting Wellbutrin for unapproved uses such as weight loss, as part of its $3 billion settlement.

title: A generic that was not equivalent
description: After patients reported it working less well, the FDA found Teva’s Budeprion XL 300 mg did not release the drug like the brand. It was pulled; the 300 mg dose had been approved on studies of the 150 mg dose.

title: Off-label promotion and kickbacks
description: GSK’s civil settlement resolved claims that it promoted Lamictal, Advair and Zofran for unapproved uses and paid doctors to prescribe them.

title: Pay-for-delay without cash
description: Buyers alleged GSK paid Teva to delay generic Lamictal by promising not to launch its own cheaper version. An appeals court ruled such non-cash deals can break antitrust law, and a class was certified in 2018. We could not confirm the final outcome.

maker: Sanofi; Abbott (now AbbVie) in the US
title: Depakote marketed for dementia
description: Abbott pleaded guilty. It had a sales force marketing Depakote to nursing homes to control agitated dementia patients, an unapproved use.

maker: Sanofi; Abbott (now AbbVie) in the US
title: France: manslaughter investigation
description: Sanofi was formally placed under investigation over claims it did not adequately warn about the risk to unborn children. Sanofi contests it.

maker: Sanofi; Abbott (now AbbVie) in the US
title: France: class action
description: In the first ruling of its kind, a Paris court found Sanofi failed in its duties of care and information. Working out compensation was expected to take years.

title: "Doctor for a day"
description: Outside doctors were paid to accompany sales reps and promote Topamax for unapproved psychiatric uses.

title: Generics that released the drug too slowly
description: After reports that they worked less well, the FDA found Mallinckrodt’s and Kudco’s generic Concerta released the drug more slowly late in the day, and stopped treating them as interchangeable with the brand.

title: Overstated benefits
description: Prosecutors said Shire promoted Adderall XR for uses lacking clinical support and overstated its efficacy over other ADHD drugs. Shire did not admit wrongdoing.

title: Misleading claims about abuse
description: Prosecutors said Shire’s sales staff made misleading statements about Vyvanse’s abuse potential, although no Shire study had concluded it could not be abused. The $56.5 million settlement also covered Adderall XR.

maker: Lundbeck; Forest/Actavis in the US (now AbbVie)
title: A forced switch blocked
description: Actavis planned to stop selling twice-daily Namenda as generics approached, pushing patients to a once-daily version with longer patents. On a New York lawsuit, a court ordered it to keep the old version on sale, and the appeals court agreed it likely broke antitrust law.
sources: Arnold & Porter (2015) <https://arnoldporter.com/en/perspectives/publications/2015/06/20150601_antitrust_alert_second_circuit__11888>; AMA Journal of Ethics (2015) <https://journalofethics.ama-assn.org/article/legal-test-pharmaceutical-company-practice-product-hopping/2015-08>

title: Gambling verdict
description: A Minnesota federal jury awarded $8.2 million, mostly punitive, against Boehringer Ingelheim and Pfizer to a patient who developed pathological gambling on Mirapex. Many other cases settled confidentially.

title: Off-label promotion
description: Cephalon pleaded guilty to promoting Provigil and two other drugs for unapproved uses.

title: Record pay-for-delay settlement
description: Cephalon paid four generic makers about $300 million to delay cheaper Provigil. Its $1.2 billion settlement with the FTC was the agency’s largest.

title: EU pay-for-delay fine
description: The European Commission fined Teva and Cephalon for a deal that delayed generic modafinil.

title: UK: excessive pricing
description: The UK competition regulator found Pfizer raised phenytoin’s NHS price by 780–1,600% after a deal with Flynn Pharma. The fine was quashed, re-imposed in 2022 and upheld by the Competition Appeal Tribunal.

title: Nitrosamine impurity
description: Pfizer recalled Chantix after tablets were found to contain N-nitroso-varenicline, a nitrosamine impurity, above the acceptable limit.

title: Buyers’ settlement
description: US consumers and insurers who paid for Chantix in 2015–21 settled for $44 million, preliminarily approved in June 2026. Pfizer denies wrongdoing.

title: Kickbacks to doctors
description: Takeda settled False Claims Act allegations that it made improper payments to doctors to induce Trintellix prescriptions.

title: Speaker-programme kickbacks
description: Biohaven allegedly paid doctors speaker fees and bought them lavish meals to induce prescriptions of Nurtec.

maker: Sanofi and Bristol Myers Squibb (now generic)
title: Lied to the FTC about a Plavix deal
description: BMS pleaded guilty to making false statements. A senior executive had made a secret side-promise to the generic maker Apotex and hid it from the FTC. The CEO was ousted.

maker: Sanofi and Bristol Myers Squibb (now generic)
title: Australia: the Commonwealth’s PBS claim
description: Sanofi won an injunction blocking Apotex’s generic on a patent later found invalid. The Commonwealth sued for what the PBS overpaid in the meantime, but lost in the High Court in December 2024 because it could not prove a generic would have been listed.

maker: Sanofi and Bristol Myers Squibb (now generic)
title: Hawaii: reduced effect in some patients
description: Hawaii argued that BMS and Sanofi knew Plavix worked less well in many East Asian and Pacific Islander patients but did not update the label. After court awards of $834 million and $916 million, the companies settled for $700 million.

title: A faulty monitor in the key trial
description: The BMJ reported that Janssen withheld problems with the INRatio device, used to adjust warfarin doses in the comparison group of the ROCKET AF trial, from the FDA. Falsely low readings could have inflated bleeding on warfarin. The companies denied it, and a reanalysis found no significant effect.

title: Bleeding lawsuits
description: About 25,000 US lawsuits over bleeding risks were settled for $775 million, split between Bayer and J&J, without admission of liability.

title: Bleeding lawsuits
description: Boehringer agreed to pay about $650 million to settle roughly 4,000 US claims over inadequate warnings of severe bleeding, saying the claims lacked merit.

title: Unshared analyses on blood tests
description: A BMJ investigation said internal analyses found fivefold variation in blood levels and that monitoring could cut major bleeds by 30–40% compared with warfarin, but these were not shared with doctors or regulators. Boehringer disputed this.

title: Altered records in the key trial
description: BMS told the FDA that a site manager in Shanghai and a contractor had altered records to hide problems in the ARISTOTLE trial. FDA documents showed concerns about data from many China sites; one official wrote the application would have been refused had the agency known earlier. Reviewers concluded the main results were not substantially changed.

title: Justice Department investigation
description: Prosecutors demanded documents about the PLATO trial after critics pointed to inconsistencies, including much of the benefit coming from two countries. The department later closed the investigation with no action.

title: New questions about the data
description: A BMJ investigation, using trial records obtained under freedom of information, reported problems with how PLATO’s data were reported. The trial’s investigators have defended the results.

maker: Novartis; generics from many makers, including Zhejiang Huahai
title: Japan: manipulated research
description: University studies claiming extra benefits for Diovan were found to rest on manipulated data, and a Novartis employee had secretly helped with the statistics. A court accepted the data were manipulated but acquitted, ruling that a paper is not an advertisement.

maker: Novartis; generics from many makers, including Zhejiang Huahai
title: A probable carcinogen in generic batches
description: NDMA was found in valsartan ingredient from Zhejiang Huahai, linked to a 2011 manufacturing change, triggering recalls worldwide. The FDA banned imports from the plant and issued a warning letter.

maker: Novartis; generics from many makers, including Zhejiang Huahai
title: Contamination lawsuits
description: US lawsuits over contaminated valsartan, losartan and irbesartan were grouped in a New Jersey federal court in 2019. Small buyer settlements with some makers were provisionally approved in 2026; Teva reported 231 personal-injury cases against it, with trials expected no earlier than 2027.
sources: JPML transfer order (2019) <https://www.jpml.uscourts.gov/sites/jpml/files/MDL-2875-Initial_Transfer-01-19.pdf>; Teva quarterly report (2026) <https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000818686/000119312526323619/d118828d10q.htm>

maker: Merck originally; now many generic makers
title: Nitrosamine recalls
description: After valsartan, the FDA found the probable carcinogens NDEA and NMBA in some losartan and irbesartan batches, leading to recalls. Not all lots were affected.
sources: FDA: ARB recalls <https://www.fda.gov/ARBrecalls>; American College of Cardiology (2019) <https://acc.org/Latest-in-Cardiology/Articles/2019/01/07/12/42/Heart-of-Health-Policy-Additional-ARBs-Added-to-FDA-Recall-List-Due-to-Contamination>

maker: Merck originally; now many generic makers
title: Part of the contamination lawsuits
description: Losartan claims are part of the New Jersey federal litigation over contaminated blood-pressure drugs, which was still running in 2026.

maker: Sanofi originally; now many generic makers
title: Nitrosamine recalls
description: Regulators in the US and UK recalled batches of irbesartan after testing found possible contamination with NDEA.

maker: Sanofi originally; now many generic makers
title: Part of the contamination lawsuits
description: Irbesartan claims are part of the New Jersey federal litigation over contaminated blood-pressure drugs, which was still running in 2026.

title: Off-label promotion
description: Boehringer settled claims that it promoted Micardis for early diabetic kidney disease, and three other drugs for unapproved uses, without admitting liability.

title: ENHANCE: results delayed
description: Investors sued after Merck and Schering-Plough sat on the ENHANCE trial for about two years. It showed Vytorin did no better than cheap simvastatin at reducing artery plaque.

title: Pay-for-delay settlement
description: Buyers alleged Merck’s 2010 patent deal with Glenmark delayed generic Zetia and included a promise not to launch its own cheaper version. Merck settled on the eve of trial.

title: Medicaid "best price" fraud
description: Merck labelled deep hospital discounts on Zocor, Vioxx and Pepcid as "nominal" prices to keep them out of Medicaid rebate calculations, and allegedly paid doctors disguised as training fees.

maker: Generic makers including Teva and Glenmark
title: Price-fixing
description: Teva and Glenmark admitted conspiring with rivals to raise the price of pravastatin and other generics. They paid $225 million and $30 million and had to sell their pravastatin businesses.

title: US insulin pricing lawsuits
description: States, cities and other payers allege that Lilly, Novo Nordisk and Sanofi raised list prices in step while paying bigger rebates to the pharmacy-benefit managers CVS Caremark, Express Scripts and OptumRx. About 514 cases were grouped in a New Jersey federal court by July 2026. The companies deny wrongdoing, and none has been found liable.

title: US insulin pricing lawsuits
description: Lilly is a defendant in the grouped US cases alleging insulin list prices were inflated in a rebate scheme with pharmacy-benefit managers. In 2024 Lilly agreed to cap insulin at $35 a month for Minnesota residents to settle that state’s claims.

title: US insulin pricing lawsuits
description: Novo Nordisk is a defendant in the grouped US cases alleging insulin list prices were inflated in a rebate scheme with pharmacy-benefit managers. It denies wrongdoing.

title: Stomach-paralysis lawsuits
description: Cases claiming GLP-1 drugs caused gastroparesis, ileus or bowel obstruction were grouped in a Pennsylvania federal court in February 2024, with about 3,760 cases by June 2026. In 2025 the judge ruled that gastroparesis claims need objective testing.

title: Vision-loss lawsuits
description: A separate group of cases over NAION, a sudden loss of vision, was set up in late 2025, with about 110 cases by mid-2026.

title: Stomach-paralysis lawsuits
description: Lilly’s Mounjaro and Zepbound are among the drugs in the grouped US cases claiming GLP-1 medicines caused gastroparesis or bowel obstruction.

title: Stomach-paralysis lawsuits
description: Trulicity is among the GLP-1 drugs named in the grouped US cases over gastroparesis and bowel obstruction.

title: Thyroid warning downplayed
description: Novo Nordisk settled allegations that sales reps gave doctors misleading information about the FDA-required warning on a rare thyroid cancer.

title: Nitrosamine above the limit
description: Tests found the nitrosamine NTTP in sitagliptin products. To avoid a shortage, the FDA temporarily allowed up to 246.7 ng a day instead of 37 ng, judging the added cancer risk minimal. Merck added quality controls.

title: Bladder-cancer lawsuits
description: In 2014 a jury found Takeda had hidden cancer risks and awarded $9 billion in punitive damages against Takeda and Lilly, later cut to $36.8 million. Takeda then settled about 9,000 cases.

maker: Many makers; Synthroid by Knoll (later Abbott, now AbbVie)
title: A suppressed study
description: A university study funded by Synthroid’s maker found generic and brand thyroxine interchangeable, potentially saving about $356 million a year. The company blocked publication for years; it appeared in JAMA in 1997. Knoll then agreed to pay at least $98 million to settle class actions, without admitting wrongdoing.

maker: Advanz Pharma (formerly Concordia) in the UK
title: UK: excessive pricing
description: The CMA fined Advanz and its former owners for overcharging the NHS for liothyronine tablets. The Competition Appeal Tribunal upheld the finding in 2023 and the Court of Appeal refused a further appeal in 2025.

maker: Auden Mckenzie and Actavis UK in the UK
title: UK: excessive pricing
description: The CMA found Auden Mckenzie and Actavis UK charged the NHS excessive and unfair prices over a decade: from under £1 to over £70 a pack, taking NHS spending from about £500,000 a year to over £80 million. The Court of Appeal later upheld the findings.

title: Heart-attack lawsuits
description: Chicago juries awarded $150 million and $140 million in punitive damages, finding AbbVie misled about cardiovascular risks; both were later retried. AbbVie signed a master settlement covering existing claims in 2018.

title: "Sham" patent lawsuits
description: A court found AbbVie filed baseless patent suits to keep generic testosterone gel off the market and ordered $448 million in relief. The appeals court upheld the wrongdoing in 2020 but struck the money.

maker: URL Pharma, then Takeda, in the US
title: An old drug, a new monopoly
description: After URL Pharma ran trials and won FDA approval for Colcrys, cheap unapproved colchicine was removed from the US market. The price rose from about $0.09 to about $5 a tablet, and a study later linked the rise to worse gout control.

title: Ghostwritten science
description: About 1,500 documents unsealed in lawsuits by more than 14,000 women with breast cancer showed Wyeth hired DesignWrite to draft more than 50 peer-reviewed papers, which promoted unproven benefits and played down risks.

title: Blood-clot lawsuits
description: By mid-2012 Bayer had paid about $403 million to settle roughly 1,900 lawsuits, and set aside more for thousands of others, without admitting wrongdoing.

title: Blood-clot lawsuits
description: Merck agreed to pay $100 million to resolve US lawsuits alleging it failed to warn of NuvaRing’s higher clot risk, denying fault.

title: Perforation lawsuits thrown out
description: About 1,300 federal cases claiming the device moved and perforated the uterus were dismissed after the judge rejected the plaintiffs’ experts; the appeals court affirmed. Bayer later reportedly paid $12.2 million to settle remaining claims.

title: Brain-pressure lawsuits thrown out
description: A separate group of cases claiming Mirena caused raised pressure in the skull was dismissed because the plaintiffs could not prove it was the cause.

title: Brain-tumour lawsuits
description: About 3,500 or more cases were grouped in a Florida federal court in 2025. Pfizer has argued US regulators would not have allowed a warning; Daubert hearings were held in mid-2026 and the first bellwether trial is scheduled for 7 December 2026.
sources: US District Court, N.D. Fla. <https://flnd.uscourts.gov/node/1421>; Anapol Weiss (2026) <https://blog.anapolweiss.com/blog/the-depo-provera-mdl-where-things-stand/>

title: Sexual side-effect lawsuits
description: Lawsuits claimed Propecia caused lasting sexual dysfunction. Most plaintiffs accepted settlements; court records unsealed after Reuters intervened showed what Merck knew.

title: Suicide reports and a slow label
description: Reuters reported that by 2009 Merck knew of more than 200 reports of depression, some with suicidal thoughts, and that an FDA reviewer’s 2010 call for a suicide warning was overruled. Merck says the evidence does not support a causal link.

title: Thigh-fracture lawsuits
description: Many claims say Merck failed to warn about atypical femur fractures. In 2019 the US Supreme Court ruled judges, not juries, decide whether federal law blocks such claims. A judge then found them blocked, but in 2024 the appeals court sent the cases back again.

title: Guilty plea: kickbacks and false paperwork
description: Warner Chilcott paid doctors through sham speaker events and meals and coached them to justify prior-authorisation requests for patients who did not qualify, for Actonel, Asacol and five other drugs.

title: Off-label promotion
description: GSK’s civil settlement resolved claims that it promoted Advair for unapproved uses, including first-line use for mild asthma, and paid doctors to prescribe it.

title: Pulled to dodge rebates?
description: GSK stopped selling Flovent and launched an authorised generic just as a US cap on Medicaid rebates was removed. Johns Hopkins researchers estimated the move cost state Medicaid programs nearly $1 billion in 2024. GSK called it a business decision to preserve access.

title: Arizona consumer-fraud lawsuit
description: Arizona’s attorney general sued, alleging GSK switched to the authorised generic to avoid paying Medicaid rebates.

title: A boxed warning, 22 years on
description: The FDA required its strongest warning about serious neuropsychiatric events, including suicidal thoughts and actions, and advised against using it for mild allergies.

title: Injury lawsuits
description: Families have sued Merck and Organon claiming inadequate warnings. Courts have split: some claims were thrown out as pre-empted by federal law, one was allowed to proceed, and Merck won another on summary judgment.

title: EU: misleading patent offices
description: The European Commission found AstraZeneca gave patent offices "deliberately misleading" information to extend Losec’s protection and withdrew products to block generics. Upheld by the EU Court of Justice in 2012.

title: Kidney-injury lawsuits
description: AstraZeneca paid $425 million to settle US lawsuits claiming Prilosec and Nexium caused kidney disease, saying the claims lacked merit.

title: Kidney-injury lawsuits
description: Takeda faced more than 6,100 US lawsuits claiming Prevacid and Dexilant caused kidney injury, and settled them in 2024 for an undisclosed amount it called not material.

title: Off-label promotion
description: GSK’s civil settlement resolved claims that it promoted Zofran for unapproved uses, including pregnancy nausea.

title: Birth-defect lawsuits thrown out
description: A judge ruled the claims were pre-empted because the FDA, fully informed, had rejected the proposed birth-defect warning; the appeals court agreed in 2023.

maker: Asacol: Warner Chilcott (later Allergan, now AbbVie)
title: Guilty plea: kickbacks
description: Warner Chilcott pleaded guilty to health-care fraud over kickbacks and false prior-authorisation paperwork covering Asacol, Actonel and five other drugs.

title: Hiding a discount from Medicaid
description: Bayer pleaded guilty. It sold "private label" Cipro and Adalat to the insurer Kaiser cheaply and did not report it as its best price, short-changing Medicaid rebates.

title: Paying a rival to wait
description: In a 1997 deal Bayer paid Barr about $398 million to hold off its generic Cipro until the patent expired. California buyers sued; Bayer settled for $74 million and Barr later for $225 million, after the state’s Supreme Court revived the case in 2015.

title: Tendon-rupture lawsuits
description: A Minneapolis federal jury awarded $1.8 million to a man whose Achilles tendons ruptured after a short course. J&J went on to win other trials among thousands of cases.

title: The missing trial data
description: After a campaign of more than four years by Cochrane and the BMJ, Roche released all 77 clinical study reports. The review found no good evidence that Tamiflu reduces hospital admissions or complications. The UK alone had spent about £424 million on stockpiles.

title: The "delayed safer drug" lawsuits
description: More than 20,000 plaintiffs alleged Gilead slowed development of its TAF-based drugs to keep selling TDF. A lower court let the claims proceed in 2024, but in August 2026 California’s Supreme Court ruled 6–1 that drugmakers have no general duty to bring an alternative drug to market sooner.

title: Speaker-programme kickbacks
description: Gilead settled whistleblower claims that lavish speaker events and fees, including more than $20 million in speaker fees, induced doctors to prescribe Biktarvy, Descovy and other HIV drugs.

title: $84,000 a course
description: An 18-month Senate Finance Committee investigation found Gilead set the price to maximise revenue, and that broad, affordable access was not a key consideration. Medicare spent $8.2 billion on Sovaldi and Harvoni in 18 months.

title: Price-fixing guilty pleas
description: Heritage’s former chief executive and president pleaded guilty to conspiring to fix the prices of doxycycline hyclate and the diabetes drug glyburide. Heritage entered a deferred prosecution agreement and paid $7.1 million in a civil settlement.

title: Free "nurse ambassadors"
description: A whistleblower case claimed AbbVie gave doctors free nurse services and other perks to drive Humira prescriptions. Settled with California’s Insurance Commissioner without admitting wrongdoing.

title: Patents, price and tax
description: Congressional investigators found Humira’s US list price rose about 470% and executive bonuses were tied to Humira revenue. AbbVie’s 132-patent "thicket" kept US biosimilars out until 2023, five years after Europe; courts found this legal.

maker: Amgen in the US; Pfizer elsewhere
title: A patent wall to 2029
description: An appeals court upheld two Amgen patents running to 2028 and 2029, blocking Sandoz’s approved biosimilar. Sandoz argued Amgen had acquired the patents from Roche to stretch protection.

maker: Amgen in the US; Pfizer elsewhere
title: Sandoz antitrust suit
description: Sandoz sued Amgen in Virginia, alleging it extended its monopoly by buying and using patent rights, and seeking triple damages.

title: Locking out a cheaper copy
description: Pfizer sued in 2017, alleging J&J tied Remicade discounts to insurers and providers shunning biosimilars such as Inflectra. The case settled confidentially in 2021, without a ruling.

title: Copay kickbacks and price-fixing
description: Teva allegedly paid Medicare patients’ Copaxone copays through charities while raising its price. The settlement also covered generic price-fixing claims.

title: Speaker and consulting kickbacks
description: Biogen settled claims that it paid doctors speaker and consulting fees to prescribe Avonex, Tysabri and Tecfidera, without admitting liability. The whistleblower pursued the case after the government declined to join.

title: Off-label promotion
description: Celgene settled a whistleblower case alleging off-label cancer promotion of Revlimid and Thalomid and payments to doctors, denying wrongdoing.

title: Generic volume limits
description: Under patent settlements, generic makers could sell only a small, slowly rising share of Revlimid’s volume until January 2026. Buyers allege a conspiracy to monopolise; in September 2026 a New Jersey judge refused to dismiss the claims against Celgene, Teva and others.

title: India: "evergreening" rejected
description: The Supreme Court of India upheld the rejection of a patent on a crystalline form of imatinib, finding Novartis had not shown it worked better than the known substance. Cheap generics continued in India.

title: Italy: Avastin/Lucentis collusion
description: Italy’s competition authority found Roche and Novartis colluded to steer eye doctors away from Avastin. Upheld after the EU Court of Justice ruled in 2018.

title: France: fine overturned
description: France fined Novartis, Roche and Genentech €444 million in 2020 for similar conduct, but the Paris Court of Appeal annulled it in 2023.

title: Permanent hair-loss lawsuits
description: Thousands of cases claimed Sanofi failed to warn of permanent hair loss. Juries cleared Sanofi in 2019 and 2021, thousands of cases were dismissed, and there has been no global settlement.

title: Eye-injury lawsuits
description: A separate group of cases claims docetaxel caused chronic tearing and blocked tear ducts. In 2026 some generic makers won, while cases against Sanofi continued.

title: Guilty plea: off-label doses
description: Amgen pleaded guilty. It had promoted Aranesp at higher doses than the label allowed, and for cancer patients not on chemotherapy, uses that later proved dangerous.

title: Misleading efficacy claims
description: Genentech and OSI allegedly told doctors Tarceva worked for lung-cancer patients who had smoked or lacked an EGFR mutation, with little evidence.

maker: Mylan (now Viatris); made by Pfizer’s Meridian
title: Misclassified to dodge rebates
description: Mylan classified EpiPen as a generic to pay smaller Medicaid rebates while raising the two-pack price from about $100 in 2007 to about $600 in 2016.

maker: Mylan (now Viatris); made by Pfizer’s Meridian
title: Antitrust class action
description: Buyers alleged a pay-for-delay deal with Teva delayed a generic EpiPen. Pfizer settled for $345 million in 2021 and Viatris for $264 million in 2022, without admitting liability.

title: Bowel-disease lawsuits
description: Juries awarded plaintiffs between $2 million and $25 million in some trials, but New Jersey’s Supreme Court dismissed 532 claims in 2018, holding that FDA-approved warnings are presumed adequate.

title: "Renting" a tribe’s immunity
description: Allergan sold its Restasis patents to the Saint Regis Mohawk Tribe, which licensed them straight back, claiming tribal immunity from patent challenges. Courts rejected the tactic, and Allergan settled buyers’ antitrust claims.

title: Off-label promotion
description: Allergan pleaded guilty. It promoted Botox for headache, pain and other unapproved uses, paid doctors to sit on "advisory boards" and created a supposedly independent education group.

maker: Generic makers including Taro and Sandoz
title: Price-fixing
description: Taro admitted conspiring with Sandoz to allocate customers and fix prices of generic drugs including clobetasol, under a deferred prosecution agreement. It paid a further $213 million in a civil settlement in 2021; Sandoz paid $195 million in 2020.
sources: Faruqi & Faruqi <https://www.faruqilaw.com/blog/564/taro-agrees-to-pay-205-million-to-resolve-price-fixing-charges>; Taro annual report (2022) <https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/906338/000095017022012998/taro-20220331.htm>; CNBC (2020) <https://www.cnbc.com/2020/03/02/novartis-subsidiary-sandoz-to-pay-195-million-over-antitrust-allegations.html>
